title: Don't Waste 2026 on the Wrong Career (Software vs AI Engineer)
summary: Career chat comparing software and AI engineering: skills, degrees, pay, interviews, convergence.

assertions.quote: people who tell you that you don't need machine learning fundamentals is wrong

verdicts.note: ML intuition helps with evals, retrieval and fine-tuning, but much LLM application work is software and data engineering; not strictly required for entry.

assertions.quote: if you're just trying to become a big tech software engineer, it's not necessary as it once was

verdicts.note: Many employers dropped degree requirements, but in the tight 2024-26 market most entry-level hires still have CS degrees; a degree is not required but still helps a lot.

assertions.quote: It's definitely going to replace tasks

verdicts.note: Through 2026 evidence points to role change and slower junior hiring, not elimination of the profession; long-run is uncertain.

assertions.quote: eventually software engineering and AI engineering is going to become the same thing

verdicts.note: A long-range prediction about job titles; cannot be evaluated now.

assertions.quote: feature development type interview ... access to AI coding tools

verdicts.note: Some companies allow AI or changed formats (e.g. Meta AI-enabled rounds), but LeetCode-style screens remain common.

assertions.quote: forward deployed engineers ... Very very hot role

verdicts.note: FDE postings grew several-fold in 2025 as AI labs and startups (OpenAI, Anthropic, Palantir-style firms) hired for them; still a small share of jobs.
Compensation data (Levels.fyi, 2025) show a premium for AI/ML engineering roles, though ranges overlap heavily.
